headline: High risk of filesystem conflict and cascading misuse: Mentat’s diff-based coding workflow can collide with nullclaw’s writable shared workspace and broad tool access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads files passed on the command line and proposes edits from file content; nullclaw can read/write workspace files and uses MCP/browser/web channels. A shared filesystem or copied content can therefore carry attacker-controlled instructions into either agent. This is not proven by direct interaction evidence, so uncertainty is resolved upward to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF either agent ingests file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP for the pair unless needed
Require explicit human review of any file-derived instructions
Prefix untrusted content with a non-executable marker
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys; nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and workspace files, and can expose them through webhooks, memory, and logs. If they share files or credentials, either agent can leak sensitive material to external services by default. The pairwise path is plausible from profiles alone, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same secrets file or workspace
IF either agent forwards file contents or memory to its configured model/API backend
mitigations: Store secrets outside any shared workspace
Rotate any credentials exposed to either agent
Restrict outbound network destinations
Audit logs and webhook payloads for secret material
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret scoping

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state, and Mentat explicitly shares state via filesystem while nullclaw supports durable shared memory plus git and spawn/tooling. Concurrent edits to the same repo can overwrite each other or corrupt git state without locking. The overlap is direct and dangerous in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF concurrent sessions modify git state without an external lock
mitigations: Run agents on separate clones
Serialize git writes with a lock file
Review and merge diffs manually
Pause one agent before the other writes
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and nullclaw has broader action surfaces including shell, browser, webhooks, and scheduling. If nullclaw treats Mentat’s output as authoritative, a mistaken edit plan can cascade into commits, web actions, or other irreversible operations. The interaction is plausible and the blast radius is large, so high is appropriate.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes Mentat’s proposed diffs without verification
IF nullclaw is allowed to execute shell or webhook actions based on those diffs
mitigations: Require a human approval step before execution
Compare proposed diffs against tests or lint output
Limit nullclaw to read-only mode during review
Log and diff all downstream actions
requires-engineering: add schema validation for Mentat outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat is a coding assistant touching source code and model-provider keys, while nullclaw handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, conversation history, memory, audit logs, and webhook payloads. Their retention and residency policies are not documented here, so a mismatch could create compliance gaps on the same data class. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as customer PII or secrets is processed by both agents
IF their logging or retention settings differ on the same workspace data
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Disable retention of sensitive logs where possible
Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Review residency and DPA terms for both services
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
